correspondence.component_scope: Selected beginning south of 56 degrees north, westward bend and northeastward approach to the P.3626 southern edge.
correspondence.finding: The retained regional index shows Hosea Lake and a named Black Duck drainage in the wider headward area. Its generalized linework does not resolve the actual selected southern feeder and connector. The selected geometry is orientation only. No passage through Hosea Lake, named source lake, continuous wetland connector or complete initial channel correspondence is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern P.3626 edge near 56 degrees north through the predominantly northward middle valley.
correspondence.finding: The original sheet directly labels the meandering trunk Black Duck River. It follows a narrow fluvial corridor through extensive organic-deposit lowlands, with small side channels and scattered water bodies. The selected route remains in the river valley rather than traversing a major lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle P.3626 corridor through the eastward bend and subsequent northeastward/northward reaches.
correspondence.finding: The trunk has the selected broad eastward turn followed by its northward continuation, with repeated Black Duck River labels. Mansemeigos Creek is separately labelled on the side-drainage corridor southeast of the trunk. Mistahayo Lake lies off the selected trunk to the east. The map does not support transferring either label to the selected mainstem or claiming a selected through-lake passage.
correspondence.name_limits: An exact source-to-lake itinerary for the side creek is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: P.3626 northern edge and P.3625 southern edge near 56 degrees 30 minutes north.
correspondence.finding: The separately issued detailed sheets overlap by their common latitude edge and show the same northbound Black Duck valley continuing across the seam. East Kettle River is a separately labelled western corridor; it is not relabelled as part of the selected Black Duck route.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern sheet from its southern edge through the northeastward border-adjacent lower course.
correspondence.finding: Repeated Black Duck River labels follow the selected lower trunk through broad meanders and the Manitoba–Ontario boundary setting. The sheet retains hydrographic linework on the Manitoba side even where its geological fill stops at the provincial boundary. Little Auntie Creek is separately labelled in the western side-channel network adjacent to the lower Black Duck. Oosteguanako Creek and Mintiagan Creek are separately labelled east-side regional drainage context and are not assigned to the selected trunk.
correspondence.name_limits: No exhaustive inventory or legal naming extent of individual anabranches or tributaries is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Black Duck River coastal fan immediately west of the provincial-boundary coast, west of the Pen Islands.
correspondence.finding: The directly labelled lower river leads into several coastal distributary/side-channel branches that meet the Hudson Bay shore. The selected terminal setting is that Black Duck coastal outlet. West Pen Island and East Pen Island lie farther east in the same regional coastal sheet. The observation establishes the receiving coastal setting, not one exact modern mouth-point vertex or a uniform name for every coastal branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID None
correspondence.finding: Across the detailed mapped middle/lower interval, the selected route follows fluvial channels through lowlands mapped extensively as organic deposits; the legend distinguishes bog and fen deposits. No major selected through-lake passage, reservoir or dam is established there. Hosea Lake is only retained regional headward context; its connection to this selected start remains unresolved. Mistahayo Lake is off the observed selected trunk. The absence of a mapped reservoir symbol is not a claim about every minor or present-day structure.
correspondence.reason_partial: Headward lake/wetland/channel linkage is part of the unresolved southern gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern headward opening
correspondence.finding: The selected opening begins south of Yonza’s southern neatline and enters the valley west of Cerro Caltama. The purported 5931-I catalogue target identifies another quadrant, and the independent Cerro Paruma sheet is excluded for its printed restriction. YLB supplies only regional terrain context. The complete opening-to-valley correspondence is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Caltama-west valley, Cuye and Catuyuma Pampa to southern Uyuni margin
correspondence.finding: Yonza shows local quebrada branches descending the valley west of Cerro Caltama, branches near Estancia Cuye, and local channels extending into Catuyuma Pampa. The selected line proceeds north through saline plain and into the salar. The map does not establish this through-going connector; local named quebradas are not promoted to a whole-route name. Laguna Charagua Kkota is mapped farther east along the southern margin, but no selected passage through that lagoon is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern Uyuni salt-flat interior
correspondence.finding: The chosen line runs across the salt-flat surface rather than a named mapped river, past the island setting around Cerro Chiar Kkollu and Isla Grande. The mapping supports the broad continuous salar setting, not a watercourse bearing the island names.
correspondence.name_role: receiving salt-flat terrain, not a representative river hydronym

correspondence.component_scope: West-central salt-flat turn
correspondence.finding: The selected bend is within the western/central continuous Uyuni salt flat. Detailed western sheets and the full-salar original YLB map show its relation to island relief and rocky western shore. No original source depicts the selected grid-like route as one named channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern salar passage and northern turn near Llica/Palaya
correspondence.finding: The selected route remains on the salar side of the rocky western/northwestern shore and turns near the Palaya sector. YLB supplies the continuous whole-salar context across the unavailable Llica-sheet interval. Palaya maps neighboring small lagoons and short local drainage, but does not establish that the selected line passes through or adopts their names. The 5934-II map was not recovered.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern salar eastward and southeastward passage
correspondence.finding: Caquena shows the selected interval across the broad salt flat south of the northern shore, with islands/shore relief nearby. No major through-river junction or named trunk is mapped for that selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Central salar continuation and actual terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward continuation and endpoint are in the central Uyuni salar surface, as read on YLB’s original gridded location map and corroborated by the monograph’s full salt-crust outline. This is an interior salt-flat terminal, without a mapped sea outlet or persistent through-river continuation. Fig.20 chemical contour curves are not waterways. The southeastern Río Grande inlet is a different mapped/prose-described tributary, not a name for this selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening, northern loop and western eastward connector
correspondence.finding: The opening and northward loop occupy the Inland Ice west and northwest of the nunatak belt. The following eastward connector continues through the interior-ice setting. The national original provides the actual local geographic reading for the portion covered by the detailed sheet’s synoptic tectonic inset, then overlaps the detailed sheet’s unobscured ice coverage.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The inset is not treated as a local map of the selected opening. No named river source or surface/subglacial flow path is inferred from ice contours or modeled connectivity.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward approach into the Wilkins Nunatakker–Eyvind Fjeld sector
correspondence.finding: After its eastward ice crossing, the selected route turns southeast toward the mapped nunatak and glacier country around Wilkins Nunatakker and Eyvind Fjeld Gletscher. The original detailed sheet distinguishes ice/perennial snow from exposed rock and undifferentiated cover throughout this connector.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: These landmarks locate the ice/land corridor; they are not transferred to the selected river, and uniform surface cover at every modeled vertex is not claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle eastward connector and lower eastward bend
correspondence.finding: The eastward middle section traverses the Eyvind Fjeld Gletscher/Jakob Kjøde Bjerg ice-and-nunatak sector and continues toward the western Waltershausen Gletscher ice field, north of the Adolf Hoel Gletscher corridor. The mapped adjoining ice passages and intervening exposed ridges account for the complete broad connector before the selected route bends south.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: A modeled line through this mixed glacier/nunatak region is not evidence that all portions form a continuous natural river, or that Eyvind Fjeld, Waltershausen or Adolf Hoel is a representative river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward lower approach and actual terminal corridor
correspondence.finding: The lower selected route bends south into the Nunatakgletscher–inner Geologfjord setting, with Andrée Land on the west side and Strindberg Land on the east side. The original distinguishes this narrow inner-fjord connection from Waltershausen Gletscher’s separate eastward/southeastward continuation to Nordfjord. The selected terminal belongs to the inner Geologfjord corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terminal-corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Historical mapped ice-front/fjord context is not a precise present-day river mouth or front survey. Retained terminal class sea is model metadata. Granitsø is a separately mapped nearby lake and is not established as a selected through-lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward reach and opening western descent
correspondence.finding: The selected model starts east of the inspected NLUIS sheets and initially trends west/southwest before turning west/northwest. Its actual starting waterbody or terrain, initial river connection, tributaries and any glacier/lake association have not been established from allowed original cartography. Model orientation alone is not correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northwestward return and northeastern Maino Lake approach
correspondence.finding: This eastern upper corridor and its return northward lie beyond the inspected sheets. The actual selected channel connections into Maino Lake, intervening lake passages and material upper tributary junctions remain unresolved. Neither regional expedition prose nor labels from search discovery establish these links.

correspondence.component_scope: Maino Lake western passage and southwest outlet
correspondence.finding: The37G southeastern corner and37F northeastern corner depict the western Maino Lake portion crossing their common boundary and continuing into the southwest-flowing Rowley valley. The lake’s eastern approach lies beyond their eastern boundary; this lake component therefore has partial original correspondence only.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest Rowley valley and tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest corridor corresponds to the broad valley labeled Rowley River below Maino Lake. Original cartography shows linked narrow/wider river reaches with rapids markings and tributaries entering from both sides. An appreciable western tributary joins before the broader middle lake sequence; unnamed lateral feeders retain unknown names.

correspondence.component_scope: Connected middle lake expansions and eastern lateral branch
correspondence.finding: The Rowley valley expands into connected irregular lakes. The selected route follows the western/southern continuation, while an eastern lateral lake and its incoming stream remain distinct adjacent components. The original shows the lake connections and the narrowing between the selected waterbody expansions; no independent lake hydronym is supplied.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward reach, eastward turn and Separation Lake
correspondence.finding: From the elongated western waterbody the mapped river turns east through a short reach with falls and rapids symbols and enters Separation Lake at its northern part. An eastern stream enters the lake system separately. The selected route turns southwest through the lake toward its outlet. The map, rather than an assumed model connector, establishes this principal lake linkage. The canoe report provides only broad falls/rapids corroboration.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Rowley River and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: Below Separation Lake, the mapped Rowley River winds west and then southwest into a narrow coastal opening on the eastern side of Steensby Inlet. The map carries the Rowley label along this outlet river. Windless Lake and its separate shoreward valley lie to the southeast and are not the selected terminal route. The foreshore/coast is generalized; no precise modern tidal limit or bank position is claimed.
